What is the atomic number of Unbihexium?
Unbihexium, also known as element 126 or eka-plutonium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has atomic number 126 and placeholder symbol Ubh.
In what year was Steve Jobs born?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year was Silver discovered?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
In what year was Manganese discovered?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.

In which country is Junkers Ju 52?
Junkers Ju 52: Germany. Development of the Ju 52 commenced in the late 1920s, headed by German aeronautical engineer Ernst Zindel.
Who is credited with discovering Plutonium?
Plutonium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
Who is credited with discovering Fermium?

Who is credited with discovering Sodium?
Sodium: Humphry Davy. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
This long-term skin condition occurs when dead skin cells and oil clog hair follicles, producing blackheads, whiteheads, and pimples mainly on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne is a long-term skin condition that occurs when dead skin cells and sebum clog hair follicles.
This large, muscular mastiff-type dog breed descends from ancestors brought to the British North American colonies, where they worked on small farms and ranches — what's the breed?
American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog.
With 1,248 built, this turboprop's design was adapted from an earlier Soviet transport aircraft and became NATO's 'Cub' — which four-engine workhorse?
Antonov An-12 (NATO reporting name: Cub) is a four-engined turboprop transport aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Once native to the highland lakes of Xochimilco and Chalco, this neotenic mole salamander keeps its external gills and stays aquatic for life — what is it?
Axolotl (from Classical; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.

The bassist of a legendary British rock band from 1962 to 1993, performing on its first 19 studio albums, this musician was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989 as part of that group — who is he?
Bill Wyman (n Perks; born 24 October 1936) is an English musician who was the bassist of the rock band the Rolling Stones from 1962 to 1993.
This rhythmic bodily process draws oxygen-rich air into the lungs and expels carbon dioxide, powering the cellular chemistry that turns food into energy — what process is it?
Breathing (respiring or ventilating) is the rhythmic process of inhaling air into the lungs providing oxygen, and exhaling the air removing carbon dioxide, in the gas exchange process.
Prized in India for hashish and cultivated from China to West Africa, this Hindu Kush-native plant produces cannabinoid levels well above ordinary hemp — which species?
Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family, this Australian parrot is recognized for its expressive crest and long tail feathers, and is a hugely popular pet bird. What bird is it?

Cockatiel (Nymphicus hollandicus), also known as the weero/weiro or quarrion, is a species of small- to medium-sized parrot belonging to the cockatoo family (Cacatuidae), of which it is the smallest member.

This family of fifteen tall, long-necked bird species mostly wears muted gray-and-white plumage with a patch of bare red skin on the face — except for one crowned genus that stands out — what bird is it?
Crane (bird) are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes.
This colourless, highly volatile, sweet-smelling organic compound with formula (CH3CH2)2O was once used as a general anesthetic and remains a common laboratory solvent — what is it?
This American physicist was the first to make a transuranium element, neptunium, sharing the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Edwin McMillan (September 18, 1907 - September 7, 1991) was an American physicist credited with being the first to produce a transuranium element, neptunium.

This branch of anthropology systematically studies individual cultures from the point of view of the people within them, relying heavily on researchers directly participating in the settings they study — what is this method called?
Ethnography is a branch of anthropology and the systematic study of individual cultures. It explores cultural phenomena from the point of view of the subject of the study.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive it combines with nearly every other element except the light noble gases. What element is it (symbol F)?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.
With the symbol Ge and atomic number 32, this lustrous, brittle metalloid was predicted to exist by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869, decades before it was actually discovered — name this element?
Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is a fisheries staple in northern Europe, often smoked into varieties like Finnan haddie and the Arbroath smokie — what is it?
Haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.

This extinct human species from the Middle Pleistocene may represent the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans — or a completely separate lineage altogether — what species is it?
Homo heidelbergensis is a species of archaic human from the Middle Pleistocene of Europe and Africa, as well as potentially Asia depending on the taxonomic convention used.
This Russian-American aviation pioneer, a trailblazer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, won the top prize at the 1912 Moscow Aviation Exhibition for one of his early designs — who is he?
Igor Sikorsky (25 May 1889 - 26 October 1972) was a Russian-American aviation pioneer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.

Designed under the philosophy 'write once, run anywhere,' this high-level, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language compiles to bytecode executed by a dedicated virtual machine — name the language?
Java (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language.
This pain-relieving, fever-reducing drug belongs to the propionic acid class of anti-inflammatories and hit the market in 1980, thirteen years after being patented — what is it?
Ketoprofen is one of the propionic acid class of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID) with analgesic and antipyretic effects.
This American computer scientist won the 2013 Turing Award for taming the chaos of distributed systems — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX — who is he?
Leslie Lamport (born February 7, 1941) is an American computer scientist and mathematician.
This paired organ, located near the backbone on either side of the heart in most mammals, extracts oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide back into it — name the organ?
Lung are the primary organs of the respiratory system in many animals, including humans.
Working on the geometry of Riemann surfaces, this Tehran-born Stanford professor became in 2014 the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal — who was she?
Maryam Mirzakhani (12 May 1977 - 14 July 2017) was an Iranian mathematician and a professor of mathematics at Stanford University.
Carrying NATO's 'Hind' codename and its crews' affectionate 'flying tank,' this Soviet machine is both an attack craft and a low-capacity troop carrier. What is it?
Mil Mi-24 (NATO reporting name: Hind) is a large helicopter gunship, attack helicopter and low-capacity troop transport with room for eight passengers.

In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature properly and never develop into healthy cells, early on there are often no symptoms, though it can progress into acute leukemia. Name the condition?
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is one of a group of cancers in which blood cells in the bone marrow do not mature, and as a result, do not develop into healthy blood cells.
This American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth bomber, solely operated by the US Air Force, is designed as a flying wing to penetrate sophisticated air defenses. What is this aircraft?
Northrop B-2 Spirit is an American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth strategic bomber, often referred to as a "stealth bomber", solely operated by the United States Air Force.
It surges during childbirth and sexual activity, drives maternal bonding and milk production, and is released by the posterior pituitary — which hormone is this?
Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
This inflammation of the lining of the abdominal cavity can be caused by a ruptured appendix, a perforated ulcer, or pancreatitis, and may lead to shock if untreated. What condition is it?
Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and often spread by flea bites, this disease comes in pneumonic, bubonic, and septicemic forms — what is it?
Plague (disease) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. There are three forms of plague, each affecting a different part of the body and causing associated symptoms.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.

One of 36 species-rich pit vipers found mainly in the Americas, this snake shakes a noisy tail segment to warn off predators and is responsible for most snakebite injuries in North America — which snake?
Rattlesnake are venomous snakes that form the genera Crotalus and Sistrurus of the subfamily Crotalinae (the pit vipers).

Known by folk names like knotberry and lowbush salmonberry, this amber fruit structurally similar to a blackberry thrives in Arctic tundra and boreal forest but isn't farmed commercially — which species?
Rubus chamaemorus (also known as cloudberry) is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
This interdisciplinary field studies signs and sign systems, breaking down into branches examining the formal relations between signs, their meanings, and their users — what's the field called?
Semiotics is the study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
This plant family includes both deadly poisonous species and kitchen staples like tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers, all linked by unusually high alkaloid content — what family is it?
Solanaceae is a family of flowering plants in the order Solanales.
In the equation 5 − 2 = 3, this is the operation being performed — which one is it?
Subtraction (which is signified by the minus sign) is one of the four arithmetic operations along with addition, multiplication and division.

This mass of gray matter forming part of the forebrain relays sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex through radiating nerve fibers, and helps regulate consciousness, sleep, and alertness — what's the structure?
Thalamus (pl.: thalami; from Greek, "chamber") is a large mass of gray matter on the lateral wall of the third ventricle forming the dorsal part of the diencephalon (a division of the forebrain).
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Its Latin name means 'maiden,' and it's the largest zodiac grouping in the sky, home to the bright star Spica between Leo and Libra — which one?
Virgo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. The ecliptic intersects the celestial equator within this constellation and Pisces.

Used to treat dangerous heart rhythms like ventricular fibrillation, which drug can take weeks to work when swallowed but carries risks of lung, liver, thyroid, and eye toxicity?
Born Fernando Martins de Bulhões, this 13th-century Portuguese Catholic priest joined the Order of Friars Minor — who is he?
Anthony of Padua: Portuguese Catholic saint (1195–1231)
This Russian designer and outspoken blogger, known for provocative and often obscene commentary, founded a namesake design studio and is a descendant of the Tolstoy family — who is he?
Artemy Lebedev: Russian designer and businessman (born 1975)
Sharing the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Tomas Lindahl and Paul Modrich, this Turkish-American scientist was honored for mechanistic studies of DNA repair — who is he?
Aziz Sancar: Turkish biochemist and molecular biologist (born 1946)
Originating in the Swiss Alps' canton of Bern, this large farm breed historically pulled carts for alpine herders and traces its ancestry to Roman mastiffs — which breed, recognized in 1912?
Bernese Mountain Dog: Swiss breed of dog. The Bernese Mountain Dog, German: Berner Sennenhund or Dürrbächler, is a large dog breed originating from the canton of Bern, Switzerland and the Swiss Alps.

Developed to supplement the 727 on short routes, this narrow-body twinjet kept the 707's fuselage width and six-abreast seating and entered service with Lufthansa in 1968 — which best-selling aircraft is it?
Patented by Roche in 1961 and approved for medical use in 1974, which benzodiazepine, similar in effect to diazepam, is sometimes given as a presurgical sedative in 1.5, 3, or 6 mg tablets?
Bromazepam: Benzodiazepine drug. Bromazepam, sold under many brand names, is a benzodiazepine.
Designated Maryland's official state crustacean, this species is expected to benefit from climate change even as overfishing hurts other Chesapeake Bay fisheries — which species?
Callinectes sapidus: Species of crustacean. It is Maryland's largest commercial fishery and has been designated its state crustacean.
A wartime myth claimed eating this vegetable helped British pilots see in the dark — really a cover story for radar — which root vegetable?
Carrot: Root vegetable. The carrot (Daucus carota subsp. sativus) is a root vegetable in the umbellifer family Apiaceae.
Holder of 186 patents, this American engineer ran research at General Motors for nearly three decades and gave the world the electric car starter, leaded gasoline, and Freon — who was he?
Charles F. Kettering: American inventor, engineer and businessman (1876–1958)
Despite its common 'cat' nickname, this small nocturnal mammal from Africa and Asia is not a feline at all — and one African species yields a musky scent long used in perfumery — what is it?
Civet: Mammals of the families Viverridae and Nandiniidae and the genus Fossa.
Greenish-brown above and off-white below, this migratory leaf warbler is named onomatopoeically for its simple two-note song — which bird?
Common chiffchaff: Small migratory passerine bird found in Europe, Asia and north Africa.
Which tart fruit ripens on trailing evergreen vines with dark pink flowers, turning from light green to red as it matures?
Cranberry: Group of plant species bearing edible fruit.
Originally developed as an antidepressant, this fast-acting SSRI was later approved to treat premature ejaculation and was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2003 — what drug is it?
Dapoxetine: Medication used to treat premature ejaculation.
Produced by the enzyme 5α-reductase acting on a more familiar male sex hormone, this compound is a more potent driver of prostate growth, sebum, and body hair — which hormone?

First imagined by Olaf Stapledon in his 1937 novel Star Maker and later named for a physicist who explored the idea in 1960, this hypothetical megastructure would encircle a star to harvest its energy — what is it?
Dyson sphere: Hypothetical megastructure around a star. A Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.
Australia's tallest native bird, this flightless species can sprint up to 48 kilometers per hour and often goes weeks without drinking water — which bird?
Emu: Large flightless bird endemic to Australia.
Every animal, plant, fungus and seaweed belongs to this domain, defined by one shared cellular feature: a nucleus wrapped in its own membrane. What are they called?
Eukaryote: Domain of life whose cells have nuclei.
Its 41 living species boast the most varied fur patterns of any land carnivore, all armed with retractile claws and an obligate taste for meat — which family is this?
Felidae: Family of mammals. Felidae ( FEE-lə-dee) is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
This infection and inflammation of hair follicles produces pimples with white tips anywhere on hair-covered skin — what is the condition called?
Folliculitis: Human and animal disease of follicles.
Native to Central Asia and a close relative of the onion, shallot, and leek, this bulbous Allium has been a seasoning and folk remedy known to Babylonians, Egyptians, and Romans alike — what is it?
This American chemist helped synthesize ten transuranium elements, dreamed up the actinide concept, and advised ten US presidents on nuclear policy — who shared the 1951 Nobel for that work?

Named for the Greek word for the sun, this element makes up about 24% of the universe's elemental mass and has the lowest boiling point of all — which colorless, odorless gas?
Helium: Chemical element with atomic number 2 (He)
German anthropologist Otto Schoetensack named this archaic human species in 1908 based on a jawbone found near the village of Mauer — then Europe's oldest known human fossil. Which species?

Homo heidelbergensis: Extinct species of archaic human. H. heidelbergensis has been regarded as either the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans; or as a completely separate lineage.
A person with this condition becomes unduly alarmed by even the most minor symptom, convinced a serious illness is upon them despite no medical diagnosis — what is it?
Hypochondriasis: Excessive fear of developing illness.
Most often extracted from chicory, this plant-stored fructan earned FDA approval as a dietary fiber in 2018 and remains the gold-standard compound for measuring kidney filtration rates — what is it?

Developed by a South Korean aerospace firm with Lockheed Martin and first flown in 2002, this supersonic jet trainer became the country's first indigenous supersonic aircraft — which aircraft family?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Family of South Korean jet aircraft. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
This plant family — home to basil, rosemary, thyme, lavender, and sage — also counts teak among its rare tree species and chia among its edible seed crops — which family?
Also called May bells or Our Lady's tears, this woodland plant's sweetly scented white bell-flowers hide a dangerously poisonous secret — which flower?
Lily of the valley: Species of flowering plant in the asparagus family.
As West Germany's economics minister, he engineered the postwar 'Wirtschaftswunder' before becoming the country's second chancellor in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard: Chancellor of West Germany from 1963 to 1966.

Despite its fox-like markings, this leggy, reddish-coated canine of the South American savanna is neither a fox nor a close relative of more familiar canines, and it plays a key role dispersing fruit seeds — what is it?

First synthesized near Darmstadt in 1982, this fleeting synthetic element — its most stable isotope lasts mere seconds — was named for the Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist Lise Meitner. Which element is it?
Meitnerium: Chemical element with atomic number 109 (Mt)
Succeeding the Castro brothers, this engineer became Cuba's first head of state in nearly six decades who wasn't a member of that family — who is he?
Miguel Díaz-Canel: Leader of Cuba since 2021.

The tallest and heaviest living species of deer, this Northern Hemisphere giant is topped in North American body mass only by the bison, and its males sport broad, hand-shaped antlers unlike any other deer's pointed racks. What is it?
Moose: Largest species of deer. It is also the tallest, and the second-largest, land animal in North America, falling short only to the American bison in body mass.
Sold as Narcan, this opioid antagonist can restore breathing within minutes of an overdose but may trigger sudden withdrawal in opioid-dependent people — what is it?
Naloxone: Opioid receptor antagonist. Naloxone, sold under the brand name Narcan among others, is an opioid antagonist, a medication used to reverse or reduce the effects of opioids.
Discovered in 1846 by Ascanio Sobrero, this oily explosive liquid became the key ingredient in dynamite — what is it?
Causing white or yellow discoloration, thickening, and lifting of the nail — and far more often striking toenails than fingernails — what is this fungal infection also called tinea unguium?
Named by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 to cover big cats of genus Panthera, this cat subfamily later grew to include the clouded leopards too — which subfamily?
Pantherinae: Subfamily of felids. The Pantherinae genetically diverged from a common ancestor between 9.32 to 4.47 million years ago and 10.67 to 3.76 million years ago.
This term describes a short chain of amino acids joined by a particular kind of bond; string together enough of them (10,000 daltons or more) and you get a protein instead — what is it?
Peptide: Short chains of 2–50 amino acids.

For two thousand years it lived inside natural philosophy alongside chemistry and biology, only breaking off as its own discipline during the 17th-century Scientific Revolution; what is this study of matter, energy, and force?
Physics: Scientific field of study. It is one of the most fundamental scientific disciplines.
First domesticated some 5,000 years ago on the Iranian plateau, this fruit-bearing shrub reached California in 1769 via Spanish settlers — which fruit?
Pomegranate: Fruit-bearing deciduous shrub. Pomegranate was first domesticated by ancient Iranians in the Iranian plateau and nearby regions about 5,000 years ago.
Created in the early 18th century, this dark pigment was the first modern synthetic color, made by oxidizing iron ferrocyanide salts — what is it?
Prussian blue: Synthetic pigment. Prussian blue (also known as Berlin blue, Brandenburg blue, Parisian and Paris blue) is a dark blue pigment produced by oxidation of ferrous ferrocyanide salts.
Element 88 reacts with nitrogen rather than oxygen in air, turning black, and once glowed in self-luminous paints despite being highly carcinogenic — which element is it?
Radium: Chemical element with atomic number 88 (Ra)
Curving around the chest, these bones protect the lungs and heart and, in snakes, support and protect the whole body — what are they called?
Rib: Long bone in vertebrates that protects vital respiratory and cardiovascular organs.
Originally conceived as a jet trainer before its role expanded to supersonic strike and reconnaissance, this Anglo-French attack aircraft is today flown only by the Indian Air Force. What is it?
SEPECAT Jaguar: French/British attack aircraft. It was also later license produced by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited in India for use of the Indian Air Force.

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Better known by the brand name Viagra, this drug treats erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension, kicking in within about twenty minutes — what is it?

Sildenafil: Drug for erectile dysfunction and hypertension. Sildenafil, sold under the brand name Viagra among others, is a medication used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Native to East Asia and the world's most-grown legume, this crop becomes everything from edamame and tofu to soy sauce, nattō and tempeh — what is it?
Soybean: Legume grown for its edible bean.
Named from Greek words for 'twisted' and 'grain,' this genus of spherical bacteria divides along a single axis to form chains, unlike its grape-cluster-forming cousins — coined in 1877, what is it?
Streptococcus: Genus of bacteria. In 1984, many bacteria formerly grouped in the genus Streptococcus were separated out into the genera Enterococcus and Lactococcus.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

A hemiparasitic plant that draws water and nutrients from host trees, this species is central to European Christmas traditions and folklore, and is now studied for possible pharmaceutical use — what plant is it commonly called?
Viscum album: Flowering plant in the mistletoe family Santalaceae.
This English economist and physician first made his name surveying Irish land to parcel out to Cromwell's soldiers, and is best remembered for his theories of 'political arithmetic' — who is it?
William Petty: English economist and philosopher (1623–1687)
